lead: Natural objects people collect—minerals, gemstones, fossils, meteorites, rocks, shells, taxidermy and other specimens, element samples and their displays—organised by scientific classification (mineral class → group → species, gem species → variety, taxon → locality/formation, meteorite class → official name, shell family → species), with dealers and gem laboratories in the brand register.

b.v: species/variety name per Mindat, GIA, WoRMS or the Meteoritical Bulletin
b.w: Each field values a piece by its accepted name first; mislabelled and trade-name stock is common.

b.v: exact locality and old collection labels > country only > none
b.w: Collectors price classic localities and documented provenance; locality is the main detail axis.

b.m: Natural vs treated, restored or fake
b.w: Dyed, heated, irradiated, reconstituted and composite pieces and casts must be disclosed.
CITES, ivory and protected-species laws and national export rules (e.g. fossils, meteorites) govern many specimens.

depts.note: Mineral class (Nickel–Strunz) → group → species → variety; ~170 popular collector species in the tree, all other species in a Mindat-linked species register.

b.v: micromount, thumbnail, miniature, small cabinet, cabinet, museum
b.w: Standard collector size classes used by dealers and shows.

b.v: damage-free, sharp, lustrous, well-placed on matrix > dinged or repaired
b.w: Mineral dealers and competition judging criteria.

s.brief: Kind = mineral species (IMA name, Mindat-linked). Under each species add archetypes for named varieties and classic locality types (e.g. a famous mine or district habit), ordered by significance; versions = notable localities/finds with years; dt = habit, size class (thumbnail, miniature, small cabinet, cabinet, museum), matrix, colour, fluorescence, treatments. Source each archetype from Mindat, Wikipedia or a museum/reference page. Quartz absorbs the crystal-shop varieties: rock crystal, amethyst, citrine (note heated amethyst), smoky, rose, ametrine, Herkimer diamond, Japan-law twin; geodes and points as dt. Agate gets classic agate types (Lake Superior, Laguna, Botswana, Fairburn, Condor, Dryhead, crazy lace); jasper named jaspers (ocean, picture, Biggs; note that 'bumblebee jasper' is a trade name for a volcanic rock). Opal: precious vs common, Coober Pedy, Lightning Ridge, Yowah, Ethiopian Welo, hyalite.

k.brief: Merge of rock crystal, amethyst, rose, smoky and citrine kinds; varieties become archetypes.
Chrysoprase, carnelian, onyx, blue lace as chalcedony varieties.

Note legality in each kind (CITES, ivory bans, migratory-bird and protected-species laws; antique/pre-Convention papers). Archetypes = named forms and recognised maker traditions (e.g. Victorian cased birds; Rowland Ward, Peter Spicer, Van Ingen, Walter Potter anthropomorphic tableaux) with sources; add tradition entries for Victorian taxidermy and Indian Van Ingen if sourced. Antlers (sheds, red deer, moose, elk), horns (kudu, ram, buffalo), tusks (warthog, hippo, walrus—legal notes; elephant ivory restricted), claws and teeth (bear claw, sperm whale tooth/scrimshaw note), shark jaws (great white restricted), eggs (ostrich, emu, elephant bird) and nests; oology legality.

Pinned Lepidoptera (Morpho, birdwings—CITES, Ornithoptera), framed vs papered (A1 grade); add Pinned beetle and other insect (Goliath beetle, Hercules beetle, rhinoceros beetle, scorpions, tarantulas); feathers (legal issues), herbarium sheets (antique pressed-plant albums), resin-embedded specimens, fluid-preserved (antique wet specimens, cleared-and-stained).

depts.note: Sample form → element; purity and mass are details.

s.brief: Element collecting hobby. Archetypes: element sets and periodic-table displays (Theodore Gray periodic table table and cards, Luciteria element cubes and sets), noble-gas glow ampoules, high-purity crystals (bismuth, gallium, osmium bead) as versions. Add Periodic table element collection (complete or partial sets in display). dt: purity, mass, size (10 mm/25.4 mm/1 in cube). Safety notes for radioactive and reactive elements.

depts.note: Cases and mounts for showing specimens.

s.brief: Restraint only: no new kinds; aliases: Riker mount → frame case; perky box, gem jar, thumbnail box → single-specimen box; acrylic risers and museum putty as types of stand. Keep a few makers only if already present.
